About AlphaSense:

AlphaSense is the AI platform redefining market intelligence and workflow orchestration, trusted by thousands of leading organizations to drive faster, more confident decisions in business and finance. The platform combines domain-specific AI with a vast content universe of over 500 million premium business documents — including equity research, earnings calls, expert interviews, filings, news, and internal proprietary content. Purpose-built for speed, accuracy, and enterprise-grade security, AlphaSense helps teams extract critical insights, uncover market-moving trends, and automate complex workflows with high-quality outputs. With AI solutions like Generative Search, Generative Grid, and Deep Research, AlphaSense delivers the clarity and depth professionals need to navigate complexity and obtain accurate, real-time information quickly. For more information, visit www.alpha-sense.com. Come join us.

About the Role

We are looking for a Director, Compensation to lead AlphaSense's global compensation function: a results-oriented leader ready to own the full compensation lifecycle, while building a high-performing team and partnering closely with the VP, Total Rewards, Finance, Legal, and business leaders across the company. We envision this highly visible, high-impact role as a strong influencer with the business and the go-to person for all things Compensation, including base pay, short-term incentives, and long-term incentives (equity).

You will lead AlphaSense's Compensation team and act as the primary owner of the company's compensation philosophy, structure, and programs. You will partner with the VP, Total Rewards on executive compensation, and serve as the owner and subject matter expert for compensation matters across the business, balancing the discipline required of a company approaching IPO with the pace and flexibility of high-growth tech.

This role requires prior experience scaling compensation functions at high-growth or newly public technology companies. A flexible, growth mindset, comfort with ambiguity and change, and successfully balancing operational excellence with a sense of urgency will be critical to success in the role.

What You'll Do

  • Strategy. Define AlphaSense's multi-year compensation roadmap in alignment with market positioning that scales with the business. Own and manage the global compensation philosophy.
  • Structural Design. Own and manage the global compensation structure across base, short-term incentives, and long-term incentives (equity), in alignment with job architecture.
  • Program Management. Own and manage broad-based compensation programs end-to-end, including Annual and Mid-Year compensation review cycles.
  • Executive Compensation. Partner with the VP, Total Rewards on the design, benchmarking, and administration of executive compensation programs. Prepare Compensation Committee materials in partnership with external advisors (e.g., Compensia), and support proxy and governance readiness as AlphaSense approaches IPO.
  • Advisory. Partner with People Business Partners, business leaders, and managers to design compelling, scalable compensation solutions by seeking to understand the desired outcome, sharing market expertise, and proposing solutions. Provide guidance on complex, high-visibility compensation matters.
  • Market Intelligence. Conduct quarterly and ad-hoc analyses to ensure external competitiveness, internal equity, and legal/pay-transparency compliance. Monitor market trends and ensure survey participation is completed to maximize our available benchmarking data set (e.g., Radford, Compa).
  • Education & Communication. Develop training and communication tools that help managers and employees understand AlphaSense's compensation philosophy, programs, and tools.
  • Governance. Partner with Talent Acquisition on new-hire offers and with PBPs on internal mobility and promotion guidelines.
  • Technology & Program Administration. Partner with the People Systems team on Workday configuration for compensation cycles, and with Payroll and Equity teams to ensure accurate transmission of payment and award data.
  • Team Leadership. Build, coach, and develop a high-performing global Compensation team, fostering a culture of ownership, operational excellence, and continuous development.

Who You Are

Required

  • Prior experience at a high-growth or newly public technology company
  • Experience owning the full global compensation function, including designing, recommending, implementing, and administering compensation programs across base pay, short-term incentives, and equity
  • Experience managing a team
  • Executive compensation experience, including exposure to Compensation Committee cadence and deliverables
  • Experience managing multiple compensation cycles in Workday
  • Strong problem-solving and data analysis skills, with comfort synthesizing data across multiple sources to support decisions
  • Demonstrated cross-functional partnership, building trust and alignment with Finance, Legal, and People Business Partners on shared, high-visibility decisions
  • Sound judgment under ambiguity, weighing risk, context, and business impact before acting, including knowing when to decide versus when to escalate
  • Exceptional results orientation with a high degree of personal initiative
  • Inclined to roll up your sleeves, with a player-coach style
  • Flexible, solution-focused attitude
  • Proactive with a bias for action
  • Growth mindset with a focus on continuous improvement
  • Comfort with ambiguity and change
  • Demonstrated success balancing operational excellence with a sense of urgency

Preferred

  • Sales compensation experience

For base compensation, we set standard ranges for all roles based on function and level benchmarked against similar stage growth companies and internal comparables. In order to be compliant with local legislation, as well as to provide greater transparency to candidates, we share salary ranges on all job postings regardless of desired hiring location. Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors including candidate experience/expertise and may vary from the amounts listed below.

You may also be offered a performance-based bonus, equity, and a generous benefits program.

Base Compensation Range

$177,000—$243,000 USD

AlphaSense is an equal-opportunity employer. We are committed to a work environment that supports, inspires, and respects all individuals. All employees share in the responsibility for fulfilling AlphaSense’s commitment to equal employment opportunity. AlphaSense does not discriminate against any employee or applicant on the basis of race, color, sex (including pregnancy), national origin, age, religion, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, military or veteran status, disability, or any other non-merit factor. This policy applies to every aspect of employment at AlphaSense, including recruitment, hiring, training, advancement, and termination.

In addition, it is the policy of AlphaSense to provide reasonable accommodation to qualified employees who have protected disabilities to the extent required by applicable laws, regulations, and ordinances where a particular employee works.

Recruiting Scams and Fraud

We at AlphaSense have been made aware of fraudulent job postings and individuals impersonating AlphaSense recruiters. These scams may involve fake job offers, requests for sensitive personal information, or demands for payment. Please note:

  • AlphaSense never asks candidates to pay for job applications, equipment, or training.
  • All official communications will come from an @alpha-sense.com email address.
  • If you’re unsure about a job posting or recruiter, verify it on our Careers page.

If you believe you’ve been targeted by a scam or have any doubts regarding the authenticity of any job listing purportedly from or on behalf of AlphaSense please contact us. Your security and trust matter to us.

About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.

The Role:

Acts as the senior Rewards Business Partner and connective layer between Nebius' global Rewards operating model and its global go-to-market organization. Owns delivery of company-wide rewards programs into GTM, ensuring effective execution, adoption, and alignment with global principles, governance, and controls. Brings deep understanding of GTM priorities, talent needs, and external market trends to proactively recommend evidence-based improvements or adaptations. Any changes are developed with global program owners and agreed through established governance, preserving one coherent Nebius operating model.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Owns end-to-end delivery of Nebius' global rewards programs for GTM, translating enterprise frameworks into clear plans, decisions, communications, and manager actions that work effectively for the organization.
  • Serves as a trusted advisor to senior GTM leaders, HR Business Partners, and Talent Acquisition, balancing strong advocacy for GTM needs with stewardship of company-wide consistency, fairness, affordability, and governance.
  • Leads evaluation of new and evolving GTM roles within Nebius' global job architecture, recommending grade, salary range, incentive opportunity, and equity treatment and escalating genuine framework gaps to the relevant global owners.
  • Leads GTM delivery across merit, bonus, and equity cycles, coordinating global timelines and requirements, guiding leadership calibrations, resolving complex issues, and ensuring accurate, equitable, and on-budget outcomes.
  • Partners with global Rewards program owners, Sales Operations, Finance, HR, and business leaders to deliver sales incentive and variable pay programs; recommends changes through governance when GTM strategy, market practice, or operational evidence shows a clear need.
  • Monitors external market trends and internal GTM workforce data across geographies, roles, pay mix, and incentive practices; identifies emerging gaps and converts the evidence into practical recommendations for global program owners.
  • Applies Nebius' global equity frameworks across GTM, ensuring consistent treatment while surfacing evidence-based proposals for geographic, performance, or critical-talent differentiation through the appropriate governance channels.
  • Develops executive insights on pay positioning, incentive outcomes, equity value, budget impact, hiring trends, and retention risk, connecting GTM-specific signals to enterprise priorities and clear decisions.
  • Tracks delivery, adoption, and effectiveness of rewards programs in GTM, identifies structural pay, incentive, compression, or equity risks, and leads corrective action with global program owners and business stakeholders.
  • Acts as the two-way bridge between GTM and global Rewards: brings business insight into enterprise design, influences priorities and practical adaptations, and translates, supports, and explains global approaches within GTM. Leads manager enablement and guides less experienced rewards professionals.

Requirements:

  • Extensive progressive experience in compensation or total rewards, including substantial business-partnering experience with Sales or other go-to-market functions in a complex multinational organization.
  • Advanced, wide-ranging knowledge of base salary, sales and short-term incentives, equity programs, market pricing, job evaluation, and annual compensation planning, with depth in GTM reward models.
  • Advanced analytical and financial modeling skills, with the ability to evaluate ambiguous variables, assess business and cost implications, and turn complex data into clear executive recommendations.
  • Demonstrated success influencing and constructively challenging senior stakeholders while balancing business advocacy with enterprise stewardship, global consistency, and sound governance.
  • Executive-level communication, consulting, and facilitation skills, with the ability to align diverse stakeholders and explain sophisticated rewards concepts with clarity and commercial relevance.
  • Experience owning delivery of cross-functional rewards programs in a matrixed global model and using compensation, market, sales incentive, and business intelligence tools to drive scalable outcomes.
  • Experience in a publicly listed, global, fast-growing technology or AI organization preferred; experience guiding other rewards professionals and a Certified Compensation Professional (CCP) designation are advantageous.

#LI-CH1

Pay Transparency

We offer competitive compensation and benefits packages. Actual compensation will be determined based on job-related factors, including experience, skills, qualifications, the level at which the candidate is hired, and geographic location, consistent with applicable law.

Base Compensation Range

$140,000—$180,000 USD

Benefits & Perks:

  • Competitive compensation
  • Career growth and learning opportunities
  • Flexibility and ownership
  • Collaborative and innovative culture
  • Opportunity to work on impactful AI projects
  • International environment and talented teams

What's it like to work at Nebius:

Fast moving - Bold thinking - Constant growth - Meaningful impact - Trust and real ownership - Opportunity to shape the future of AI

Equal Opportunity Statement:

Nebius is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fostering an inclusive and diverse workplace and to providing equal employment opportunities in all aspects of employment. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy), national origin, ancestry, age, disability, genetic information, marital status, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

Applicants must be authorized to work in the country in which they apply and will be required to provide proof of employment eligibility as a condition of hire.

If you need accommodations during the application process, please let us know.

People Partner

Hello, I’m Danielle, Senior Director, People Experience at Customer.io! We're expanding our people team in the United States and seeking a People Partner to support our global team in a fast-paced, innovative environment. This is a great fit for an HR professional with a few years of experience who's ready to deepen their impact as a partner to the business.

The People Partners at Customer.io are advocates for our people, leveraging their skills in data analytics, change management, and industry knowledge. They use these skills to enhance Customer.io’s transformation, agility, and efficiency, delivering meaningful outcomes for both our team members and the business.

You'll work alongside a cross-functional team to support talent management, development, retention, and organizational effectiveness. Strong communication, critical thinking, and a foundation in workforce planning will set you up for success. If you're passionate about contributing to a supportive, high-performing culture, we'd love for you to join our collaborative team.

About Customer.io

Over 8,000 companies — from scrappy startups to global brands — use our platform to send billions of emails, push notifications, in-app messages, and SMS every day. Customer.io powers automated communication that people actually want to receive. We help teams send smarter, more relevant messages using real-time behavioral data.

Some things you'll do:

  • Support business alignment: Partner with departmental leaders to understand business needs and help develop plans that build organizational capabilities and support growth.
  • Performance management: Own and elevate our review cycles end to end — lead the annual and bi-annual processes, guide calibration and compensation decisions, and coach managers to build accountability and develop talent across the team.
  • Employee relations: Guide managers and employees through day-to-day questions and concerns with fairness and sound judgment, fostering a positive, respectful work environment.
  • Organizational development: Help assess team structures and work with leaders to identify areas for improvement and put changes into practice.
  • Change management support: Support organizational change efforts and help build change-readiness across teams.
  • Leadership support: Build strong working relationships with managers to understand their needs in the context of business goals, and provide day-to-day partnership and guidance.
  • Data analysis: Review and analyze People metrics and analytics (including employee experience and lifecycle data) to spot trends and support informed decisions.
  • Employee engagement: Work with leaders to roll out engagement initiatives.
  • People programs support: Help develop and implement people programs that foster employee growth and development.
  • People team support: Be an active member of the People Experience team, contributing to strong HR capabilities.

About you:

  • You're a self-starter with strong communication and presentation skills.
  • You've got a knack for creative problem solving and avoid a one-size-fits-all approach.
  • You're a champion for change, supporting leaders and employees through change initiatives.
  • You care about employee engagement, team members' well-being, and DEIB, and are eager to help build programs that support them.
  • You understand the importance of tailoring programs, strategies, and suggestions to fit different needs.
  • You're agile and adaptable, with a growth mindset for learning new skills.

What we're looking for:

  • HR Experience: 5+ years of progressive HR/People experience, ideally as an HRBP or People Partner supporting multiple teams or functions. You bring real depth across organizational design, change management, performance management, DEIB, culture championing, coaching and development, and people programs such as rewards and recognition. A strong foundation in People data and analytics — using metrics to diagnose issues and drive decisions — is especially important for this role.
  • Business Acumen: Ability to understand performance objectives that drive business outcomes, and to leverage data and analytics to support informed business decisions.
  • Experience with Management: Experience partnering with leaders and demonstrating influence and accountability in support of the people agenda.
  • Global Perspective: Ability to establish trust, fairness, and credibility with team members, managers, and cross-functional partners in a global environment.
  • Collaborative Problem Solver: Ability to work seamlessly with key partners across the People Team, including Recruiting, People Operations, and Total Rewards.

Compensation & Benefits

We believe in transparency. We are offering a compensation package between $100k - $130k USD, subject to market rate adjustment. In addition to base salary, this role includes an equity grant in the form of stock options, so you share in the success you help build.

We know our people are what make us great, and we’re committed to taking great care of them. Our inclusive benefits package supports your well-being and growth, including 100% coverage of medical, dental, vision, mental health, and supplemental insurance premiums for you and your family. We also offer 16 weeks paid parental leave, unlimited PTO, stipends for remote work and wellness, a professional development budget, and more.

See full benefits here →

Our Process

No gotchas, no trick questions - just a clear, human process designed to help both of us make an informed decision.

  1. 30-minute video call with a Recruiter
  2. 45-minute video call with the Hiring Manager
  3. 45-minute video call with the Business Leader, Compensation Leader and 2 People Partner Team Members
  4. Take-Home Assignment + 60-minute Panel Presentation with the People Team Leadership

All final candidates will be asked to complete a background check and employment verifications as part of our pre-employment process.

Customer.io recognizes the stifling impact of systemic injustice on diverse communities. We commit to using our influence to increase inclusion and equity within the tech industry. We strive to build an inclusive team culture, implement bias-free hiring practices, and develop community partnerships to expand our global impact.

Zoom is the only video conference platform that we use, virtual interviews will be conducted using the video capability (i.e., not via the chat), and offers will be extended in writing on official Customer.io letterhead. Please be vigilant in all of your job search activity, and if you have any questions please contact jobs@customer.io.

Join us!

Check out our careers page for more information about why you should come work with us! We are passionate about our core values of Empathy, Transparency, Responsibility, and Awkwardness and are looking for new coworkers to share and build that passion!

jobs.jobDescription:
About ElevenLabs

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always.

We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:

  • ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

  • ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

  • ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.

How we work

  • High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

  • Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

  • AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

  • Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

  • Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.

What we offer

  • Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

  • Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

  • Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

  • Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

  • Annual team offsite: Each year, we bring your entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia, Italy and Cancún

  • Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

About The Role
We're scaling from 1,000 → 4,000 employees across 50+ countries, and the complexity of our teams, hubs, and workflows is growing quickly. Our People Partners play a critical role in enabling leads, supporting peeps, and protecting performance and culture as we grow. As a People Partner at ElevenLabs, you'll sit at the intersection of leadership coaching, performance, and day-to-day people guidance.

You'll support Engineering and Product leaders across our international teams, getting to know their rhythms, challenges, and talent needs. Much of the role is coaching: helping leads handle feedback, performance, growth, and change well, and surfacing people issues early. You'll work as part of the wider People team, with Employee Relations and People Ops alongside you on more complex cases.

This is a high-impact role for someone who enjoys coaching, can context-switch quickly, builds trust easily, and brings clarity and calm to fast-moving environments.

You will

  • Partner with Engineering and Product leaders across our international teams to support team health, performance, and talent density.

  • Coach leads and managers through people challenges, including feedback, performance, conflict, growth conversations, and team change.

  • Run proactive 1:1 sessions mainly with leads, and with peeps where needed, surfacing issues early.

  • Contribute to organisational design work, advising on team structures, spans and layers, and capability gaps.

  • Support leaders and teams through change, such as team moves and new ways of working.

  • Support key People programs (performance reviews, engagement, recognition, and lead enablement) for Engineering and Product.

  • Work with Employee Relations and, where required, Legal Counsel on early-stage ER issues, escalating complex cases.

  • Spot patterns across teams and share them with the wider People team to shape new People initiatives.

  • Work with People Ops & Compliance teams to support terminations, mobility, and local requirements in each country where needed.

Requirements

  • Experience supporting leaders and teams through people topics such as performance, coaching, growth, and team change.

  • Strong coaching skills, with the confidence to guide managers through difficult conversations.

  • Strong judgment and the ability to handle sensitive issues with discretion, clarity, and fairness.

  • Ability to thrive in a high-velocity, ambiguous environment and make decisions with incomplete information.

  • Comfortable with both partnership and hands-on execution when needed.

  • Comfortable working with leaders across different timezones and cultures; experience supporting globally distributed or multi-jurisdiction teams is a strong plus.

  • Experience supporting Engineering or Product teams.

Location

This role is remote-first, so it can be executed from anywhere in on the East Coast USA or Europe

#LI-Remote

We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability or other legally protected statuses.

jobs.jobDescription:
Canonical is a leading provider of open source software and operating systems to the global enterprise and technology markets. Our platform, Ubuntu, is very widely used in breakthrough enterprise initiatives such as public cloud, data science, AI, engineering innovation and IoT. Our customers include the world's leading public cloud and silicon providers, and industry leaders in many sectors. The company is a pioneer of global distributed collaboration, with 1200+ colleagues in 75+ countries and very few office based roles. Teams meet two to four times yearly in person, in interesting locations around the world, to align on strategy and execution.

The company is founder led, profitable and growing.

Canonical builds the open-source software that runs the world’s clouds, devices and AI, and we hold our managers to a high standard. Our Talent Development team exists to make leaders and managers at Canonical genuinely excellent. We define what great management looks like here, and we put that standard into the hands of managers and leaders across the company.

The Organisational Development Associate is where our most driven early-career people begin. From day one you work with real teams and take on real change, coached hard by senior practitioners on a fast path toward running this work yourself. This is not a support or back-office role, and it is not generalist HR. We hire for potential, drive and coachability over a polished CV, and we back the people we hire to move fast.

Applying to this role will enter you into our People Track for consideration across roles in the function.

Location: These are remote based positions, available across EMEA and the Americas.

The role entails

  • Being embedded inside a real team: see how it works day to day, and surface what is and isn't working.
  • Running the diagnostics on a team's health and management effectiveness (engagement, 360, direct feedback), and turning the evidence into a clear, honest read.
  • Owning an improvement end to end: a concrete change to how a team works that you design, drive and land, with a senior practitioner alongside you.
  • Supporting managers in delivering effective 360 performance feedback to individuals and helping them turn it into two or three real commitments they follow through on.
  • Helping build the playbook: the standards, tools and shared language the whole function runs on. You are building the system others use, not producing filler.
  • Learning coaching and organisational development directly from senior practitioners, on a fast, visible path to running this work yourself.

What we are looking for in you

  • A track record of leading and organising early. You have run things, built things, won people over and made change happen, in a startup, a student society, the military, a team, anywhere. People around you already see you as a driver.
  • A deliberate pull toward developing people and organisations. You chose this field on purpose, with a real grounding in organisational or industrial psychology, behavioural science or a comparable basis. It is not a fallback.
  • Drive and eagerness to learn. You have your own ideas and the confidence to challenge, and you are hungry to be coached and to grow fast.
  • The presence to sit across from experienced people and talk about change with confidence.
  • An exceptional academic track record from high school and university.
  • Up to around two years of experience since graduating.
  • Business level written and spoken English.
  • Organised, accurate, confident, authentic, results-oriented, and enthusiastic.
  • Sincere personal motivation aligned with our mission.
  • Willingness to travel up to 4 times a year for internal events.

In addition we expect that you will match our values, by being:

  • Precise, taking care to deliver correctness and clarity.
  • Reliable, delivering high quality work that builds trust and confidence.
  • Accessible, collaborating to build products and systems that are usable.
  • Adroit, blending enthusiasm, knowledge, adaptability, style and character.

Nice-to-have skills

  • Any exposure to people, organisational, coaching or consulting work, through study, an internship or a first job.
  • A genuine interest in the craft of management and organisations, not just the subject matter.
  • Comfort working with data.

What we offer colleagues

We consider geographical location, experience, and performance in shaping compensation worldwide. We revisit compensation annually (and more often for graduates and associates) to ensure we recognise outstanding performance. In addition to base pay, we offer a performance-driven annual bonus. We provide all team members with additional benefits, which reflect our values and ideals. We balance our programs to meet local needs and ensure fairness globally.

  • Distributed work environment with twice-yearly team sprints in person.
  • Personal learning and development budget of USD 2,000 per year.
  • Annual compensation review.
  • Recognition rewards.
  • Annual holiday leave.
  • Maternity and paternity leave.
  • Employee Assistance Programme.
  • Opportunity to travel to new locations to meet colleagues.
  • Priority Pass, and travel upgrades for long haul company events.

About Canonical

Canonical is a pioneering tech firm at the forefront of the global move to open source. As the company that publishes Ubuntu, one of the most important open source projects and the platform for AI, IoT and the cloud, we are changing the world of software. We recruit on a global basis and set a very high standard for people joining the company. We expect excellence - in order to succeed, we need to be the best at what we do. Most colleagues at Canonical have worked from home since its inception in 2004.​ Working here is a step into the future, and will challenge you to think differently, work smarter, learn new skills, and raise your game.

Canonical is an equal opportunity employer

We are proud to foster a workplace free from discrimination. Diversity of experience, perspectives, and background create a better work environment and better products. Whatever your identity, we will give your application fair consideration.

#LI-remote

  • Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

  • Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

  • Annual team offsite: Each year, we bring your entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia, Italy and Cancún

  • Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

About the role

We're scaling from 1,000 → 4,000 employees across 50+ countries, and the complexity of how we support our people through performance, conflict, and change is growing quickly. Our Employee Relations (ER) Partners protect fairness, consistency, and trust as we grow. You'll own our most sensitive and complex People cases, so that leads can act early.

As an ER Partner at ElevenLabs, you'll lead formal performance processes, investigations, grievances, and disciplinary matters from start to finish, working closely with Legal and outside counsel across many jurisdictions. You'll also coach leads through difficult conversations before they become formal cases, and turn what you see into playbooks, frameworks, and training that reduce risk and case volume over time.

This is our first ER hire. We're building a dedicated ER function, and we want someone who can help shape and build it out: how cases are triaged and escalated, how we work with counsel, and how we measure what's working.

This is a high-impact role for someone who can handle sensitive situations with discretion, make sound judgment calls, and bring clarity and calm to fast-moving environments.

You will

  • Lead formal performance processes, including back on track plans, end to end, in partnership with Leads and People Partners.

  • Run fair, well-documented investigations into misconduct allegations, grievances, and complaints, from fact-finding through to outcome.

  • Manage disciplinary, dismissal, and exit matters, drafting outcomes and communications with Legal.

  • Partner with in-house employment counsel and, when necessary, outside counsel to assess risk.

  • Triage incoming cases with People Partners using clear escalation criteria, so the right cases reach ER at the right time.

  • Keep the case log and report on patterns, risks, and trends by team, region, and case type.

  • Build playbooks, templates, and training that raise lead capability and cut avoidable cases.

  • Build out a self-serve ER flow for leads, so that common ER cases become scalable.

  • Partner with People Ops & Compliance teams to ensure smooth execution of terminations, local requirements, and compliance-heavy workflows.

Requirements

  • Hands-on experience leading employee relations cases, including performance management, investigations, grievances, and disciplinaries, ideally in a fast-growing company.

  • Strong judgment and the ability to handle sensitive issues with discretion, clarity, and fairness.

  • Solid working knowledge of employment law principles and comfort working alongside in-house and outside counsel.

  • Skilled in writing clear, defensible documentation and coaching leads through hard conversations.

  • Comfortable moving fast and staying agile, shifting priorities quickly as cases and the business change, without losing rigour.

  • Comfortable building process as well as running cases, as the ER function is still being built.

  • Experience supporting globally distributed teams or multi-jurisdiction environments is a strong plus.

Location

This role is remote-first, so it can be executed from anywhere in on the East Coast USA or Europe.

CodePath is the largest educator of college computer science students in the country. We've trained over 50,000 students from more than 1,000 universities. Our partners include Amazon, Google, and other leading technology companies. After nearly a decade of training technical talent, we launched a $150M initiative with Anthropic to prepare people for careers in AI.

We're expanding into new markets and growing our team as AI changes the workforce. People joining CodePath now will help shape this next stage of our work.

We believe technical skills create opportunities. Our goal is to train millions of learners and create lasting economic impact. If you want to build something new, take ownership, and see the results of your work, this is a place to do it.

About the Role

Location: Remote (U.S.)
Role Type: Full-Time
Reports To: Director, Early Talent, Claude Corps
Manages: Claude Corps screeners
Compensation: $110,000 to $150,000

About Claude Corps

Claude Corps is a fellowship that places early-career talent in nonprofits, government agencies, and public-interest organizations to build AI solutions those organizations can continue using after the fellowship ends. It is a partnership between Anthropic, CodePath, and Social Finance. Fellows are full-time employees for a one-year term.

Each cohort is larger than the last, and every candidate deserves a process that feels organized, responsive, and human. That’s where you come in.

You’ll lead the Claude Corps screener team day to day. You make sure applications are reviewed, screens are completed, and every candidate decision is documented on time.

The Director sets recruiting strategy and cohort hiring goals. You turn those goals into weekly targets, plan staffing, and manage the team’s work. This is a hands-on management role. You train and coach screeners, review their work, and keep selection standards consistent as volume grows. You work closely with the Director, the recruiting coordinator, and the Claude Corps program team.

Key Activities

Run screening delivery

  • Turn cohort hiring goals into weekly review and screening targets with the Director
  • Assign work based on volume, deadlines, and screener availability
  • Track outstanding reviews, screens, and decisions, and flag staffing gaps early
  • Deliver a steady pipeline of qualified candidates to final-round interviews

Maintain clear selection standards

  • Train screeners on the program’s eligibility requirements, interview questions, and evaluation criteria
  • Make sure every decision has a completed scorecard with clear evidence
  • Review decisions regularly for consistency across screeners, and resolve unclear guidance
  • Use candidate and final-round results to sharpen screening guidance and questions

Build and lead the screener team

  • Hire and train screeners as cohort needs grow
  • Set clear expectations for output, decision quality, documentation, and candidate communication
  • Coach screeners with regular feedback and address performance issues directly
  • Run weekly team meetings and keep the screener guide and process instructions current

Run the operation

  • Keep Greenhouse reviews, stages, and scorecards complete and accurate
  • Give the Director weekly results, explain what’s driving changes, and recommend actions
  • Plan screening capacity ahead of application surges and share what results show about where more qualified applicants are needed
  • Use AI and automation to cut repetitive administrative work, and train screeners to check the quality of what it produces
  • Keep people responsible for evaluating candidates and making selection decisions

Key Success Metrics

  • Weekly delivery: Application reviews and screens meet agreed targets, and delays and staffing gaps are flagged early
  • Selection quality: Screeners apply criteria consistently, with clear evidence in every scorecard
  • Screener readiness: New screeners are trained in time for cohort needs and meet the team’s standards
  • Accurate reporting: The Director gets reliable weekly numbers with context and recommended actions
  • Team performance: Screeners get regular feedback, and performance issues are addressed promptly

Qualifications

  • You have at least five (5) years of recruiting experience, including managing recruiters or screeners in a high-volume or early-talent hiring program
  • You have managed a team’s workload, output, and quality using weekly targets and reporting
  • You have trained people to apply consistent selection standards and can explain how you checked their decisions
  • You have coached team members and addressed performance issues directly
  • You have personally reviewed applications and conducted structured candidate screens at volume
  • You can manage candidate stages, scorecards, and reports in an applicant tracking system (Greenhouse experience is preferred)
  • You use AI in your work and can describe a process you improved or automated
  • You can build clear processes while a program is still developing and adjust them as needed

Full-Time Employee Benefits

This is a 100% remote position—work from anywhere in the U.S.! CodePath prioritizes employee well-being with a competitive benefits package to support your health, financial security, and work-life balance.

  • Health & Wellness: Medical, dental, and vision insurance (90% employer-covered for employees and dependents), employer-funded healthcare reimbursement, FSAs, and Employee Assistance Program
  • Financial Security: 401(k), employer-paid life & disability insurance, and identity theft protection
  • Work-Life Balance: Generous PTO, paid holidays, 10 weeks of fully paid parental leave, and an annual year-end company closure (Dec 24 – Jan 2)
  • Professional Growth: $1,000 annual professional development stipend and home office setup support
  • Student Loan Forgiveness: CodePath is a qualifying employer for Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF), helping employees manage student loan debt
  • Additional Perks: Pet wellness plans, legal services, home/auto insurance discounts, and exclusive marketplace savings

Pay range

$110,000—$150,000 USD

Cohorts now run in the hundreds, and new fellows onboard while earlier cohorts are still placed. We need an HR partner who can support fellows and their managers year-round and run onboarding at that scale.

About the role

You are the HR partner to Claude Corps program leaders and the AI Practice Leads who manage fellows day to day. You will own onboarding quality and deadlines for each cohort while Sr People Operations Coordinator, reporting to you, runs the day-to-day execution.

Your focus shifts throughout the year. As a cohort prepares to start, you spend more time running onboarding and completing the work alongside the Sr. People Operations Coordinator. Once fellows are placed, you spend more time advising managers, addressing employee concerns, and supporting performance. New cohorts will onboard while earlier cohorts are still working, so you will need to balance both responsibilities.

This is a senior, hands-on role. You bring sound judgment to employee situations, help managers address issues early, and build clear processes as the program grows. You work closely with the Head of People, the recruiting team, program leaders, Finance, and our HR service providers.

As onboarding volume grows, you identify when additional support is needed, define that work, and train and oversee the people helping deliver it. You remain accountable for onboarding quality and deadlines.

What you’ll do

Partner with program leaders and managers

  • Advise program leaders and AI Practice Leads on performance, employee concerns, role expectations, and team needs, and help managers set clear expectations and address problems early
  • Clarify who owns what between fellow managers, host organizations, and the program team when employee questions arise
  • Identify recurring issues and recommend changes to manager guidance, policies, or how the program operates

Manage employee relations and performance issues

  • Handle employee concerns with care and consistency: gather the facts, document clearly, and bring significant issues and recommended actions to the Head of People
  • Guide managers through performance conversations, improvement plans, and conduct issues
  • Manage leave and accommodation requests with the appropriate providers and advisors

Own fellow onboarding

  • Run onboarding for each cohort, from signed offer through the employment steps needed to start: background checks, I-9 and work authorization, employee records, payroll setup, and benefits enrollment
  • Confirm work locations and coordinate state notices and employment documents
  • Send clear instructions, track each fellow’s progress, and work with recruiting and program teams to resolve missing information, changes, and delays
  • Complete onboarding tasks directly, check that records and setup are accurate, and keep employment onboarding aligned with orientation and cohort start dates

Plan and oversee onboarding support

  • Manage the Senior People Operations Coordinator: set priorities by cohort, review their work, and keep sensitive questions and decisions with the right HR owner
  • Plan onboarding workload against cohort size, deadlines, and support needed for current fellows, and flag when volume requires surge help
  • Build checklists and repeatable processes so larger cohorts onboard with less manual work

Support fellows throughout the year

  • Be an HR contact for questions about benefits, leave, workplace concerns, and employment policies
  • Help managers and fellows resolve timekeeping issues and coordinate payroll corrections with Finance and our providers
  • Maintain accurate employee records as work locations or employment details change
  • Coordinate fellowship completion, early departures, and offboarding
  • Track recurring questions and improve guidance so fellows and managers know what to do

Maintain policies and employment practices

  • Keep the Fellow Handbook, manager guidance, and state supplements current with the Head of People and appropriate advisors
  • Coordinate multistate employment requirements and help managers understand the rules for hourly, nonexempt employees
  • Apply policies consistently and seek legal or specialized advice when a situation calls for it

Improve HR processes and reporting

  • Track onboarding readiness, open tasks, and employee issues, and give the Head of People clear updates on risks, workload, and recommended actions
  • Use approved AI tools and automation to cut repetitive work in communications, tracking, and reporting, while checking accuracy and protecting employee information

Requirements

  • At least seven years of progressive HR experience, including time as an HR business partner advising managers on performance, conduct, and sensitive employee situations
  • You have personally run onboarding at volume and can move between advising leaders and doing the operational work
  • You have supported employees across multiple states, including hourly, nonexempt employees
  • You understand how HR records, payroll, benefits, leave, and onboarding connect. PEO experience is a strong plus
  • You have managed or trained staff doing HR or onboarding work
  • You can build structure in a growing program while handling overlapping deadlines and day-to-day employee needs
  • You communicate clearly, document well, and know when to involve the Head of People or a specialist
  • You have improved HR processes using technology, AI, or automation

Key success metrics

  • Onboarding readiness: Fellows complete required employment steps on time, with accurate records and payroll and benefits setup
  • Manager support: Managers receive practical guidance and address performance and employee concerns promptly
  • Employee relations: Issues are handled consistently, documented clearly, and escalated at the right time
  • Balanced delivery: New cohorts onboard on schedule while current fellows and managers continue receiving timely HR support
  • Onboarding capacity: Support needs are identified early, assignments are clear, and work is checked for quality
  • Employment practices: Policies, records, and state requirements stay current, with gaps addressed promptly
  • Process improvement: Manual work and recurring errors decrease as cohort size grows

Compensation

CodePath has standardized salaries based on the position’s level, no matter where you live. For this role, we’re hiring for a Senior level position at an annual salary of $110,000 to $150,000. Salary is determined based on your relevant experience and skills as evaluated through our interview process.

  • Health & Wellness: Medical, dental, and vision insurance (90% employer-covered for employees and dependents), employer-funded healthcare reimbursement, FSAs, and Employee Assistance Program
  • Financial Security: 401(k), employer-paid life & disability insurance, and identity theft protection

  • ​​Student Loan Forgiveness: CodePath is a qualifying employer for Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF), helping employees manage student loan debt

The role

Location: US, East Coast remote · Reports to: VP, People Foundations

You'll own Dataiku's global compensation, equity and benefits strategy. The goal: programs that win in AI talent markets, are fair inside the company, scale across 18 countries, and stay financially sustainable.

Our People function is lean and decentralized. You'll work directly with executives, Finance, Legal and the Compensation Committee, lead a small Total Rewards team, and have real autonomy. This is a builder role: you'll challenge how things are done today and use AI to reinvent how rewards work.

What you'll do

  • Set the strategy. Own and evolve our global compensation philosophy, balancing market competitiveness, internal equity and financial discipline.
  • Lead pay transparency. Define our global approach and get the company ready for new rules, including the EU Pay Transparency Directive.
  • Build the foundations. Evolve our job architecture, leveling and salary ranges, with rigor but without bureaucracy, and give managers simple tools to make good pay decisions.
  • Partner on equity. Design grant guidelines, new-hire and refresh awards, and partner with Finance and Legal on modeling, dilution and international tax.
  • Advise the top. Bring clear recommendations to executives and present equity and executive comp to the Compensation Committee and Board.
  • Run the cycles. Lead merit, promotion and incentive cycles from modeling to execution, with scalable governance and AI-enabled workflows.
  • Own global benefits. Set strategy across entities and EOR countries, and lead the benefits team that runs day-to-day operations.

What we're looking for

  • Extensive Total Rewards or compensation experience (typically 10+ years), ideally in a global, high-growth tech or enterprise software company.
  • Deep expertise in global comp strategy: salary structures, benchmarking, incentive design and job architecture.
  • Strong equity experience across countries; late-stage private company experience is a big plus.
  • Hands-on knowledge of pay transparency in Europe and North America.
  • A track record of building or transforming rewards programs, not just running them.
  • Experience leading teams and influencing senior executives in lean, fast-moving environments.
  • Strong analytical and modeling skills, and real curiosity for AI and automation (Workday a plus).

jobs.jobDescription:
ABOUT QUINCE

Quince is a destination for builders, creators, innovators, and operators who want to come together and challenge the status quo. Our mission is simple: make really high quality essentials for really low prices, fairly and sustainably. We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. We find, build relationships with, and work directly with the manufacturing partners behind some of the world’s finest products. From there, our teams design smart, efficient operational processes and build and deploy proprietary technology, AI, and analytics to help us scale fast.

What began with a small assortment of elevated basics has quickly grown into a cross-category brand spanning apparel, accessories, home goods, and more. Today, tens of millions of people across a growing number of countries come – and return – to Quince because they trust us to deliver.

OUR CULTURE

Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. We question conventional thinking, use technology and data to uncover new opportunities, and move quickly to turn ideas into reality. We aren’t interested in replicating how others do retail. We’re building a better way – at a speed and scale unlike anything that’s been done before.

  • We dream big and chase the hard problems others shy away from. Rejecting long-held assumptions is part of our company's DNA. Where conventional wisdom says you have to choose – soft or durable, speed or rigor, quality or price – we ask why that trade-off has to exist in the first place.
  • Our pace is fast and the bar is high because our customers expect a lot from us and we refuse to let them down. We believe the best results come from challenging ourselves, learning from one another, and building on each other's strengths.
  • Here, responsibility is not determined by role, tenure, or seniority. Every team member - no matter their level - has the opportunity to drive our business and shape our trajectory.

If you’re someone who likes to imagine new possibilities and build better systems rather than plug-in to outdated ones, Quince is the place for you.

THE ROLE

Recruiting Systems Administrator

We are looking for a Recruiting Systems Administrator to own the day-to-day administration and optimization of our talent acquisition tech stack. You will be the go-to expert for Greenhouse (ATS), ModernLoop (interview scheduling) and adjacent recruiting tools, including systems built in-house. You will keep these systems configured, connected, and running cleanly so recruiters and coordinators can move fast and hiring teams have a seamless experience. You will also help shape and maintain the talent tooling we build in-house. This is a hands-on role for someone who loves solving problems, tightening processes, and finding opportunities to automate repetitive work as we scale hiring across the business.

Responsibilities

  • Administer and configure Greenhouse, ModernLoop, and adjacent recruiting tools, including job templates, interview plans, scorecards, approval chains, and permissions.
  • Manage user access, roles, and permission groups across the TA stack, ensuring the right people have the right level of access and offboarding is timely.
  • Build and maintain recruiting workflows and automations that reduce manual steps for recruiters and coordinators.
  • Own data hygiene in the ATS, including deduplication, field standardization, and routine audits to keep reporting reliable.
  • Support integrations between recruiting tools and downstream systems, and partner with the Systems Engineers on troubleshooting data feeds.
  • Serve as tier-one support for recruiter and coordinator system questions, triaging issues and resolving them or escalating with clear context.
  • Coordinate with vendors on support tickets, release management, new feature rollouts, and configuration changes.
  • Document system configurations, standard operating procedures, and training materials so knowledge does not live in one person's head.
  • Identify and implement opportunities to automate recruiting operations, applying AI-enabled tooling to improve speed and accuracy.

Qualifications

  • 5+ years of experience administering recruiting or HR systems, with hands-on Greenhouse or comparable ATS administration.
  • Strong working knowledge of interview scheduling tools such as ModernLoop and their configuration.
  • Demonstrated experience managing user access, permissions, and workflow configuration in SaaS platforms.
  • A track record of improving data hygiene and building reporting-ready processes.
  • Experience supporting integrations between systems and coordinating with vendors on troubleshooting.
  • An automation mindset and comfort using AI-enabled tools to streamline repetitive operational work.

jobs.jobDescription:
Tremendous is the global platform built for businesses to send thousands of payouts to anyone, anywhere, for free. We're trusted by 20,000 organizations like Atlassian, MIT, and United Way to deliver gift cards and money to millions of recipients worldwide.

Our customers (researchers, marketers, HR teams, nonprofits, and platform businesses) rave about how fast and easy Tremendous is to use. Check out our ratings on G2.

Tremendous is profitable and growing without outside investors. We're a fully remote, high-documentation, low-meeting culture, which means more time for what matters in both your professional and personal life. The team agrees– our employee NPS is in the high 80s.

About the role

We're ~175 people across the US, Canada, the UK, Brazil, and elsewhere, and we're launching our first dedicated people function. You'll own people operations end to end, you'll be the person anyone at the company can go to when something is wrong, and you'll run our immigration program in conjunction with outside counsel.

What you'll do

  • Own our HRIS and associated systems

  • Administer benefits for US, Canadian, and international employees: open enrollment, carrier and broker escalations, HSA and FSA, COBRA, 401(k), and required annual notices.

  • Own the employee handbook, HR wiki, and people policies. Write the ones we're missing.

  • Own onboarding end to end: cohort logistics, new hire paperwork, and the first-90-days experience. Own offboarding, exit interviews, and severance logistics.

  • Be the company's HR point of contact. Take reports, run investigations, and write up findings. Build the intake, trust, and escalation process that makes reporting feel obvious and low-risk.

  • Run our biannual HR cycle — performance check-ins, compensation review, and the employee engagement survey — on schedule, and improve it each time.

  • Handle off-cycle compensation changes, promotions, relocations, and international moves, and the comp implications that come with them.

  • Partner with recruiting on international employment models (EOR, contractor)

  • Own our immigration program: manage active O-1, L-1A, H-1B, and PERM matters end to end, drive outside counsel on timelines, track renewals and expirations before they become urgent, and own I-9 compliance and verification.

  • You have excellent judgment in situations with no precedent, and you write down your reasoning.

  • You're comfortable being senior and still doing the unglamorous work. This role includes open enrollment reminders and chasing I-9 signatures.

What you'll bring

  • 5+ years in people operations, HR, or a people partner role, including time at a company without a large HR team

  • Experience independently running workplace investigations, including harassment matters, and writing defensible documentation

  • Deep experience administering US benefits and leave; global benefits experience is a bonus

  • Strong HRIS experience; Rippling preferred

  • Direct, hands-on experience with employment-based immigration: H-1B, O-1, L-1, and PERM

  • Experience running performance and compensation cycles for 100+ people

What's cool about the role

  • You're the first. You'll define what the people function is here rather than inheriting someone else's version of it, with direct access to leadership and real latitude to decide how this works.

  • Competitive pay and equity. Base salary for this role: $130k to $175k.

  • Real benefits. 100% covered health (US), unlimited PTO, 12-16 weeks paid parental leave.

  • Fully remote. Work from anywhere in the Americas.

  • Great culture. Read more about how we work in our public handbook.

jobs.jobDescription:
CodePath is the largest educator of college computer science students in the country. We've trained over 50,000 students from more than 1,000 universities. Our partners include Amazon, Google, and other leading technology companies. After nearly a decade of training technical talent, we launched a $150M initiative with Anthropic to prepare people for careers in AI.

We're expanding into new markets and growing our team as AI changes the workforce. People joining CodePath now will help shape this next stage of our work.

We believe technical skills create opportunities. Our goal is to train millions of learners and create lasting economic impact. If you want to build something new, take ownership, and see the results of your work, this is a place to do it.

Role Details

Location: Remote (US)
Role Type: Full-Time
Reporting to: Head of People
Compensation: $165,000 - $195,000

About Claude Corps

Claude Corps is a fellowship that places early-career talent in nonprofits, government agencies, and public-interest organizations to build AI solutions those organizations can continue using after the fellowship ends. It is a partnership between Anthropic, CodePath, and Social Finance. Fellows are full-time employees for a one-year term.

Each cohort is larger than the last, and every candidate deserves a process that feels organized, responsive, and human. That’s where you come in.

About the role

You’ll own recruiting and selection for Claude Corps, from finding candidates through accepted offers and the handoff to the teams responsible for onboarding and program delivery.

You set the recruiting plan for each cohort: how many fellows we need, when we need them, where we’ll find them, and how we’ll select them. You lead the team that makes it happen, hold the bar for who moves forward, and answer for hiring results to CodePath leadership and our partners.

You’ll partner across Marketing, Anthropic, the Claude Corps program team, and the AI Practice Leads, use data to guide decisions, and use AI to reduce repetitive work.

Key Activities

Set the plan and own the numbers

  • Build the recruiting plan for each cohort, covering fellows needed, timeline, sourcing, selection, staffing, and tools
  • Own the hiring forecast from application volume to accepted offers, with one weekly view of progress and risks
  • Adjust the plan as results come in and bring clear recommendations to leadership and partners
  • Keep program leadership and partners aligned on sourcing, selection, staffing, and progress toward hiring goals

Run selection

  • Manage selection from application review through accepted offer, using the program’s eligibility requirements and evaluation criteria
  • Train screeners and interviewers to apply the same standards as volume grows
  • Use hiring results to sharpen screening questions, review guidance, and interviews
  • Give candidates clear expectations, timely updates, and consistent follow-through from first contact to offer acceptance

Lead and grow the team

  • Lead the Senior Manager, recruiters, screeners, and coordinator
  • Set weekly priorities, shift work as deadlines tighten, and coach the team to the hiring standard
  • Develop leaders within the team and plan staffing for each cohort
  • Help the whole team use AI well in daily work, keeping people responsible for decisions that need judgment

Partner across the program

  • Work with Marketing on application volume and quality targets and on which sources produce qualified candidates
  • Set clear recruiting steps, response times, and handoffs with program partners and the onboarding team
  • Build processes that let the team handle larger cohorts with the same quality

Requirements

  • You have led early-talent or high-volume recruiting at scale, owning the hiring plan, candidate pipeline, team, and results
  • You can work backward from a hiring goal, track how candidates move through each stage, plan staffing, and explain why results differ from the plan
  • You have built new candidate pipelines and partnerships, and you can show which sources led to hires
  • You have built and led a team, including managing managers
  • You have improved selection processes, trained interviewers to apply consistent standards, and used recruiting tools and AI to handle more hiring while maintaining candidate quality

Key Success Metrics

  • Cohort hiring: Each cohort reaches its hiring target on time, with fellows who meet the program’s standards
  • Candidate pipeline and sourcing: Applications open early, and effective candidate sources are established for every cohort
  • Selection quality: Screeners apply the same criteria, and regular reviews and final-round results help the team improve
  • Offer acceptance: Offers go out on time, enough candidates accept to meet cohort goals, and the onboarding team receives complete information
  • Team development: Team members take on more responsibility, and managers are ready to lead as the program grows

Full-Time Employee Benefits

This is a remote position—work from anywhere in the US! CodePath prioritizes employee well-being with a competitive benefits package to support your health, financial security, and work-life balance.

  • Health & Wellness: Medical, dental, and vision insurance (90% employer-covered for employees and dependents), employer-funded healthcare reimbursement, FSAs, and Employee Assistance Program
  • Financial Security: 401(k), employer-paid life & disability insurance, and identity theft protection
  • Work-Life Balance: Generous PTO, paid holidays, 10 weeks of fully paid parental leave, and an annual year-end company closure (Dec 24 – Jan 2)
  • Professional Growth: $1,000 annual professional development stipend and home office setup support
  • Student Loan Forgiveness: CodePath is a qualifying employer for Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF), helping employees manage student loan debt
  • Additional Perks: Pet wellness plans, legal services, home/auto insurance discounts, and exclusive marketplace savings

Pay range

$165,000—$195,000 USD

jobs.jobDescription:
Canonical is a leading provider of open source software and operating systems to the global enterprise and technology markets. Our platform, Ubuntu, is very widely used in breakthrough enterprise initiatives such as public cloud, data science, AI, engineering innovation and IoT. Our customers include the world's leading public cloud and silicon providers, and industry leaders in many sectors. The company is a pioneer of global distributed collaboration, with 1200+ colleagues in 75+ countries and very few office based roles. Teams meet two to four times yearly in person, in interesting locations around the world, to align on strategy and execution.

The company is founder led, profitable and growing.

Canonical builds the open-source software that runs the world’s clouds, devices and AI, and we hold our managers to a high standard. Our Talent Development team exists to make leaders and managers at Canonical genuinely excellent. We define what great management looks like here, and we bring managers and leaders up to that standard through direct, hands-on work, both from the centre and embedded inside engineering and commercial organisations.

As a Senior Organisational Development Practitioner you are the person who sets the bar for how coaching and organisational development is practised here. You coach leaders to a clear standard of management excellence. You diagnose how a whole organisation is led and drive the plan to raise it. You develop the practitioners working in the field. It is one of the most senior and demanding Talent roles at Canonical: hands-on coaching and organisational-development craft with real leaders, in a company that expects you to be credible in a room of directors and to earn that credibility fast.

You work both from the central team and embedded inside a leader's organisation for periods, turning what you learn in the field back into how we develop leaders and managers across Canonical.

Location: These are remote based positions, available across EMEA and the Americas.

What you deliver

Raising individual leaders

  • Coaching leaders to visibly raise their game against a clear standard of management excellence.
  • Landing the hard conversations, because you coach leaders to make them happen.
  • Turning 360 feedback into real, followed-through commitments, not a report that gets filed.

Lifting organisations and the company

  • Leaving an organisation you take on visibly better led, off a sharp first-weeks diagnosis and a plan you own and drive.
  • Contributing to defining and implementing new ways of working across our globally distributed company.

Building the function and its standards

  • Developing the practitioners in the field so they get visibly better at their craft under your supervision.
  • Setting the bar for how coaching and organisational development is done at Canonical: owning what exceptional looks like, proving the methods in the field, and holding the practice to them.
  • Sharpening the management-excellence standard itself across Canonical, by feeding back what you learn in the field.

What we are looking for in you

  • Deep, hands-on coaching and organisational-development practice with real leaders and teams, not just programme design.
  • A track record of measurably changing how leaders behave, with specific examples you can talk through.
  • Credibility: you can walk into a room of directors and be taken seriously.
  • Effectiveness operating inside someone else's organisation without formal authority.
  • A clear and honest philosophy of development: you know where coaching helps, and you are candid about where a role or fit decision is the right call.
  • An exceptional academic track record from high school and university.
  • Excellent written and spoken English.
  • Sincere personal motivation aligned with our mission.
  • Willingness to travel up to 4 times a year for internal events. 

In addition we expect that you will match our values, by being:

  • Precise, taking care to deliver correctness and clarity.
  • Reliable, delivering high quality work that builds trust and confidence.
  • Accessible, collaborating to build products and systems that are usable.
  • Adroit, blending enthusiasm, knowledge, adaptability, style and character.

Nice-to-have skills

  • A management-consulting background: comfortable with ambiguity, able to diagnose, propose and move.
  • Experience coaching across a distributed, fast-moving, technical organisation.
  • Experience building competency or development frameworks.
  • Experience designing and running effective workshops or training sessions, in person and online.
  • Learning-design judgment for development materials. We want the design sense; AI handles the production drafting.
  • Talent-development experience, valued alongside but secondary to coaching and consulting craft.

What we offer colleagues

We consider geographical location, experience, and performance in shaping compensation worldwide. We revisit compensation annually (and more often for graduates and associates) to ensure we recognise outstanding performance. In addition to base pay, we offer a performance-driven annual bonus. We provide all team members with additional benefits, which reflect our values and ideals. We balance our programs to meet local needs and ensure fairness globally.

  • Distributed work environment with twice-yearly team sprints in person
  • Personal learning and development budget of USD 2,000 per year
  • Annual compensation review
  • Recognition rewards
  • Annual holiday leave
  • Maternity and paternity leave
  • Employee Assistance Programme
  • Opportunity to travel to new locations to meet colleagues
  • Priority Pass, and travel upgrades for long haul company events

About Canonical

Canonical is a pioneering tech firm at the forefront of the global move to open source. As the company that publishes Ubuntu, one of the most important open source projects and the platform for AI, IoT and the cloud, we are changing the world of software. We recruit on a global basis and set a very high standard for people joining the company. We expect excellence - in order to succeed, we need to be the best at what we do. Most colleagues at Canonical have worked from home since its inception in 2004.​ Working here is a step into the future, and will challenge you to think differently, work smarter, learn new skills, and raise your game.

Canonical is an equal opportunity employer

We are proud to foster a workplace free from discrimination. Diversity of experience, perspectives, and background create a better work environment and better products. Whatever your identity, we will give your application fair consideration.
