jobs.jobDescription:
The Workplace Engineering function sits at the intersection of traditional HR analytics and modern Product Engineering. We transform raw workforce data into a suite of "People Products" that drive high performance. We don’t just "report" on what happened; we engineer the tools and insights that determine what happens next.

This new role will report directly to the Global Head of Workplace Engineering, and sits within our Data discipline inside of our People department. Experienced data professionals at Canonical live at the intersection of software, data, and the business. They don't just help surface analytic artifacts; they help transform them into a strategic asset that elevates decision making and innovation across our global operations (e.g., sales, marketing, engineering, and human resources). They balance technical precision with business pragmatism, designing and iterating on experiments, automations, and products that transform insights into valued outcomes. They shape tomorrow's AI/Data stack in open source, ensuring that Canonical remains at the forefront of data-driven excellence. Their curiosity is contagious and has an amplifying effect on data literacy and stewardship across the business teams they support.

Location: This is a remote role based in the AMER or EMEA Region.

The role entails

  • Multi-Disciplinary Leadership: Lead and mentor a specialized squad of People Data Scientists, Software Engineers, and UX Designers. You aren't just managing analysts; you are leading a product squad.
  • Product Ownership on People Science: Bridge the gap between "HR-speak" and "Dev-speak", ensuring engineers understand the human behavioral intent behind the code.
  • Strategic Insight & Business Outcomes: Move beyond descriptive metrics (e.g., turnover rate) to predictive and prescriptive insights (e.g., predicting attrition risk based on "Time-Product" engagement data).
  • Data Stewardship & Product Storytelling: Act as the "Translator-in-Chief". Take complex data models and turn them into compelling narratives. Lead the development of AI Agents that can surface insights to managers in real-time. Ensure the "People Data Stack" is secure, GDPR/privacy-compliant, and acts as a "Single Source of Truth" across all People related offerings, products and services.
  • “Effectiveness at Work” Strategy: Identify opportunities to leverage “High Tech” solutions in our People offerings, and free up more time for “High Touch”, human involvement, thereby maximizing human value.

What we are looking for in you

  • Background in data science, mathematics, or engineering, skilled in advanced statistics, data wrangling/science, databases (SQL, etc.) or software engineering.
  • Strength in coding/scripting languages (Python, R, JavaScript, etc.), software engineering, visualization (e.g. Superset, Tableau), and automation.
  • Ability to translate business questions to key research objectives.
  • Ability to identify the best methodology to execute research, synthesize and analyze findings.
  • Proven ability to lead and drive others to execute against well planned roadmaps, with a strong mentor/coaching mindset. 
  • Willingness to examine the status quo and be resilient in the face of challenges.
  • Ambition to build tomorrow's AI/Data stack in open source.
  • An exceptional academic track record from high school and university.
  • Business level written and spoken English.
  • Sincere personal motivation aligned with our mission.
  • International travel 2-4 times a year for company events up to two weeks long.

In addition we expect that you will match our values, by being:

  • Precise, taking care to deliver correctness and clarity.
  • Reliable, delivering high quality work that builds trust and confidence.
  • Accessible, collaborating to build products and systems that are usable.
  • Adroit, blending enthusiasm, knowledge, adaptability, style and character.

Nice-to-have skills

  • Experience with Airbyte, Ranger, Superset, Temporal, or Trino
  • Basic understanding of containerization technologies such as Docker and Kubernetes
  • Agentic Engineering
  • Product management
  • User experience and design

What we offer colleagues

We consider geographical location, experience, and performance in shaping compensation worldwide. We assess performance and revisit compensation twice annually to ensure we recognize outstanding colleagues. In addition to base pay, we offer a performance-driven annual bonus or commission. We provide all team members with additional benefits which reflect our values and ideals. We balance our programs to meet local needs and ensure fairness globally.

  • Distributed work environment with twice-yearly team sprints in person
  • Personal learning and development budget of USD 2,000 per year
  • Bi-annual compensation review
  • Company recognition rewards
  • 40 days annual leave per annum, including public holidays and our All Company holiday periods
  • Maternity and paternity leave
  • Team Member Assistance Program & Wellness Platform
  • Opportunity to travel to new locations to meet colleagues, with Priority Pass for lounge access

About Canonical

Canonical is a pioneering tech firm at the forefront of the global move to open source. Our platform, Ubuntu, is very widely used in breakthrough enterprise initiatives such as public cloud, data science, AI, engineering innovation, and IoT. Our customers include the world's leading public cloud and silicon providers, and industry leaders in many sectors. We are founder-led, profitable, and growing.

Powered by worldwide distributed collaboration since our inception in 2004, we believe tech and business leadership can emerge anywhere. We have no central headquarters. Most of us work from home, but we are exceptionally disciplined about this. We have very high expectations of all colleagues, and are champions of excellence. Working here is a step into the future and will challenge you to think differently, work smarter, learn new skills, and raise your game.

Canonical is an equal opportunity employer

We are proud to foster a workplace free from discrimination. Diversity of experience, perspectives, and background create a better work environment and better products. Whatever your identity, we will give your application fair consideration.

jobs.jobDescription:
About Toptal

Toptal is a global network of top talent in business, design, and technology that enables companies to scale their teams, on-demand. With $200+ million in annual revenue and team members based around the globe, Toptal is the world’s largest fully remote workforce.

We take the best elements of virtual teams and combine them with a support structure that encourages innovation, social interaction, and fun. We see no borders, move at a fast pace, and are never afraid to break the mold.

Position Description

We are seeking a highly versatile and experienced Sales Recruiter to join our dynamic team. In this role, you’ll partner closely with our Sales leaders to strategically attract and hire top-tier sales talent across all levels - from individual contributors to VP level.

As a key member of our Recruiting team, you’ll act as a true business partner - collaborating with leadership to define search strategies and serving as a trusted advisor to help interview teams hire effectively and efficiently. We are looking for someone who is passionate about delivering world-class candidate experiences, has a strong track record of hiring top sales professionals, and thrives in a collaborative environment. You will own full life-cycle recruiting efforts, influence strategy, and help shape how we attract and engage high-performing candidates.

This is a remote position. However, candidates must be located in the United States or Canada. We do not offer visa sponsorship or assistance. Resumes and communication must be submitted in English.

Responsibilities:

The following information is intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed. It is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, or required skills.

  • Build and maintain a strong pipeline of highly qualified candidates for all Sales roles, partnering closely with Executive and Sales Leadership teams to ensure hiring goals are met.
  • Proactively source, identify and engage top-performing talent across global markets.
  • Conduct thorough candidate outreach and screening across multiple channels, effectively communicating role details while continuously assessing candidate fit.
  • Design and coordinate customized interview processes that align with Toptal’s high hiring bar and role specific requirements.
  • Act as the primary point of contact for candidates, guiding them through each stage of the interview process and ensuring an exceptional candidate experience.
  • Communicate effectively and consistently with internal teams via Slack and Zoom.

In the first week, expect to:

  • Onboard and integrate into Toptal through virtual introductions and Zoom coffees with colleagues.
  • Review team playbooks, processes, and best practices to build a solid foundation for success.
  • Dive into our Applicant Tracking System, exploring its full functionality along with the tools and systems we use daily.

In the first month, expect to:

  • Gain a clear understanding of our success criteria and begin shaping your hiring strategy.
  • Review Recruiter call recordings to understand our approach and develop your Toptal pitch.
  • Start sourcing for our sales roles while building strong relationships with Hiring Managers to align on needs and expectations.
  • Begin guiding candidates through the recruitment process - from initial outreach to offer acceptance.

In the first three months, expect to:

  • Have successfully hired your first candidate.
  • Fully own the recruitment lifecycle - from sourcing to offer acceptance, while exercising discretion and independent judgment.
  • Contribute direct feedback and insights to support continuous team and process improvement.

In the first six months, expect to:

  • Build strong, scalable candidate pipelines to support rapid hiring for high-impact sales roles.
  • Develop deep relationships with key stakeholders across the sales function, acting as a trusted business partner to support their growth and success.
  • Coach and support interviewers to strengthen evaluation practices and elevate the overall candidate experience.

In the first year, expect to:

  • Serve as a subject matter expert in sales recruiting, confidently guiding decision-making and answering questions across all stages of the sales hiring lifecycle.
  • Lead or contribute to strategic initiatives that improve our sales recruiting function - whether optimizing processes, enhancing tools, or driving innovation to help us attract top-tier sales talent at scale.

Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree is required.
  • 5+ years of proven success in recruitment, with at least part of that experience in-house.
  • Minimum of 3 years of sales recruiting experience, with a focus on hiring high-performing, enterprise-level sales talent.
  • Experience recruiting from professional services environments, particularly candidates with a track record in enterprise-level, complex solution selling.
  • Experience hiring for roles that require P&L ownership and a strong understanding of business operations.
  • Experience partnering with Hiring Managers to strategically guide them through the end-to-end recruiting process for sales roles.
  • You bring a team-first mindset - you’re humble, curious, adaptable, and always willing to pitch in wherever needed to help the team succeed.
  • You’re a proactive talent hunter; you don’t wait for candidates to come to you.
  • You have a strong ability to recognize exceptional talent and assess whether candidates will thrive in both the role and the company as it scales.
  • You extend offers with confidence, knowing you’ve built trust and alignment throughout the process.
  • Detail-oriented and organized, your candidate pipelines are clean, your communications are timely, and no loop is ever left open.
  • A compelling storyteller - you know how to excite sales candidates and clearly communicate Toptal’s value proposition.
  • Open to feedback and focused on continuous improvement, both individually and as a team.
  • You prioritize by impact and operate with focus and attention in a fast-moving, rapidly-scaling tech environment where quality and speed are both essential.
  • Able to work independently and effectively in a remote, fast-paced setting.
  • A sharp eye for the traits that make someone an outstanding contributor on a global, remote sales team.
  • Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills - you deliver a high-touch, high-quality experience for candidates and hiring managers alike.
  • You must be a world-class individual contributor to thrive at Toptal. You will not be here just to tell other people what to do.

Essential Job Functions

  • Regularly and reliably attend scheduled virtual team meetings on camera.
  • Work independently with minimal supervision.
  • Use all required digital collaboration tools.
  • Prioritize and self-manage workflows and deadlines.

US FLSA Classification: Full-Time/Exempt

This position receives a base salary and is also eligible to receive a discretionary bonus. For candidates who meet the qualifications and job requirements listed above, individual pay is determined by work location and additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

Applications are accepted on an ongoing basis. In the US, Toptal’s benefit offerings include participation in a 401(k) retirement plan; medical, dental, and vision health insurance plans; basic life insurance coverage and short-term and long-term disability coverage; access to flexible spending, dependent care, and health savings accounts; access to telehealth virtual doctors; an employee assistance program; and flexible paid time off.

About the role

As Sr. Director of Global Compensation, you will lead the design, execution, and evolution of Veeam’s global compensation framework — supporting our talent acquisition goals and strengthening employee engagement in a competitive market.

Partnering with business leaders across the company, as well as colleagues in People Partnering, Talent Acquisition, HR Technology, Finance, and Legal, you will be our subject matter expert on compensation strategy — advising senior stakeholders on key initiatives and leading programs across compensation planning, benchmarking, job architecture, performance management, cost modeling, annual cycles, and M&A.   • Develop and implement competitive compensation practices across our global workforce, including salary structures, incentive plans, and equity programs
  • Design and administer compensation programs: annual salary reviews, short- and long-term incentives, equity refreshes, and promotions
  • Keep compensation programs compliant with internal policies and federal, state, and global regulations, and lead our readiness for pay transparency rules, including the EU Pay Transparency Directive
  • Anticipate compensation risks and pay equity gaps before they surface, and put guardrails in place to prevent them
  • Model costs and impact for new or changing programs, using AI and advanced analytics in modeling, benchmarking, and program design, and set how the team applies those tools

  • Command of the EU Pay Transparency Directive and comparable pay equity regimes — you lead job leveling, gap reporting, and multi-country transparency readiness, not just monitor it

jobs.jobDescription:
CodePath is the largest educator of college computer science students in the country. We've trained over 40,000 students from 1,000+ universities, and our partners include Amazon, Google, and other leading technology companies. We've spent nearly a decade training the next generation of technical talent, and we just launched a $150M initiative with Anthropic, building one of the most ambitious AI workforce programs in the world.

We're now expanding into new markets and scaling our team so we can move at the speed AI is transforming the workforce. People joining CodePath now will have the opportunity to help architect the next frontier of our work.

We believe technical skill is the fastest way to turn raw talent into real opportunity. We train the engineers the AI era runs on, building toward millions of learners, hundreds of millions in revenue, and billions in economic impact. If you want to own something and be part of a 0-to-1 journey at an organization moving at the speed of AI, this is the place to build it.

About the Role

Team: People
Reports to: Head of People
Location: Remote (US)
Type: Full-time
Compensation: $175,000 - $200,000

Why This Role, Now

CodePath is hiring across product, engineering, growth, curriculum, and revenue at the same time, and the quality of every one of those hires runs through Talent Acquisition. We have proven we can generate demand. Our next challenge is building a hiring engine that reliably turns that demand into great hires: a clear bar at every stage, enough qualified candidates in every pipeline, and a team equipped to move quickly without lowering the standard.

This is the senior leader who owns that engine. You will define CodePath's talent acquisition strategy, build and scale the team that runs it, and sit at the table with our senior leadership on the decisions that shape the company. You will report to the Head of People and own recruiting outcomes across the organization.

What You Will Own

The talent acquisition strategy. You set the vision for how CodePath attracts, evaluates, and hires talent, and you translate the company's growth plans into a workforce and hiring plan the organization can execute against.

Pipeline and throughput at scale. You are accountable for the volume and quality of candidates across every open role. Every search reaches a strong slate of finalists, sourced and inbound work together, and no role stalls for lack of qualified candidates.

Build a team that scales. You will grow talent acquisition from a lean team into a function built for scale. You decide the shape of the org, hire and develop the recruiters, sourcers, and managers who run day-to-day recruiting, and size capacity to the hiring load rather than react to it. You set the operating rhythm that keeps hiring on track as the team grows.

The hiring system. You own the process end to end: the rubrics, the interview stages, the scorecards, and the gates that decide who advances. You make sure every stage produces real signal, so that decisions are trustworthy before we ask them to be fast.

Employer brand and market presence. You own how CodePath shows up to candidates. You build the brand and the always-on talent pools that bring strong people to us, so the function does not run on outbound alone.

The executive partnership and the numbers. You partner directly with the senior leadership team and hiring managers on role definition, calibration, and decisions. You own the recruiting narrative to executives and the board, pairing the numbers with the action being taken and the next step. You also own TA's budget, tooling, and vendor strategy.

What Success Looks Like in Your First Year

In your first 30 days, you will map the funnel end to end, meet every hiring manager and senior leader, and put a diagnosis and a plan on the table: where signal and volume break down, and exactly how you will fix each.

By 90 days, every stage carries a defined purpose and a hard bar, interviewers are trained and cannot interview until they are, hiring managers are on a cadence they do not get to skip, and your team plan is approved with hiring underway.

By the end of your first year, every open role runs with a full slate of strong finalists, time to hire drops because the process makes good decisions the first time, employer brand pulls qualified candidates to us instead of us chasing them, and CodePath has a talent function that scales ahead of the company's growth instead of racing to catch up.

Who You Are

  • You have 10 or more years in talent acquisition, including experience leading the function through a period of real growth.
  • You have built or rebuilt a hiring function, not just run one. You can point to the strategy you set, the process you changed, and the outcomes both produced.
  • You lead with data. You know your funnel math, you can name your conversion rates by stage, and you use them to decide where to invest and how to size the team.
  • You hold a high bar on quality and can defend it under pressure to move faster. You understand that compressing a process that is not yet producing good signal only reaches bad decisions sooner.
  • You have built and scaled a recruiting team, not just managed one. You have hired recruiters and managers, designed the org, and grown headcount to match a rising hiring load.
  • You are credible with executives and the board. You can push back with respect, hold the line on process, and keep senior stakeholders aligned on a shared bar.
  • You use AI as a genuine multiplier on the mechanical parts of recruiting, and you have a clear point of view on where human judgment has to stay in the loop.
  • "You are hands-on today. Your recent work has you inside a team, personally owning outcomes, not primarily advisory, fractional, or consulting engagements you hand off to someone else to run."
  • "You bring visible urgency to this work. You want to get in and personally fix what is broken in the first 90 days, not just describe what you would advise someone else to do."

Nice to Have

  • Experience owning talent across technical and non-technical functions at once (engineering, product, growth, operations).
  • Fluency with Greenhouse, Gem, and LinkedIn Recruiter, and a track record of choosing and running the TA tool stack.
  • Experience in a high-growth startup or a mission-driven organization.
  • A history of building employer brand and always-on talent pools that draw candidates in.

How We Work

We recruit AI-first. AI clears the busywork so that human judgment on candidates gets more attention, not less. We expect you to set the standard for how the team uses these tools, and to have a clear view on where they help and where they do not belong. We value leaders who adopt new tools because they want to work better, not because someone told them to.

Why Join

You will own and build a function, with the mandate and the executive support to do it right. Your work will directly determine the caliber of people who carry CodePath's mission forward, which means it directly determines how many students reach a career in tech that would otherwise have been out of reach.

Compensation

CodePath standardizes salaries by level, no matter where you live. Salary within this band is determined by the relevant experience and skills you demonstrate through our interview process.

Full-Time Employee Benefits

This is a 100% remote position, work from anywhere in the U.S. CodePath prioritizes employee well-being with a competitive benefits package to support your health, financial security, and work-life balance.

  • Health & Wellness: Medical, dental, and vision insurance (90% employer-covered for employees and dependents), employer-funded healthcare reimbursement, FSAs, and Employee Assistance Program
  • Financial Security: 401(k), employer-paid life & disability insurance, and identity theft protection
  • Work-Life Balance: Generous PTO, paid holidays, 10 weeks of fully paid parental leave, and an annual year-end company closure (Dec 24 to Jan 2)
  • Professional Growth: $1,000 annual professional development stipend and home office setup support
  • Student Loan Forgiveness: CodePath is a qualifying employer for Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF), helping employees manage student loan debt
  • Additional Perks: Pet wellness plans, legal services, home/auto insurance discounts, and exclusive marketplace savings

Pay range

$175,000—$200,000 USD

You'll be expected to ask good questions, form a point of view, and present it - not just execute a task list.

  • Take a loosely defined problem and turn it into a clear plan: what you're solving, what you need to know, and how you'll get there.
  • Research, synthesize, and structure complex information into something a busy executive can act on.

About GiveDirectly

What if the most effective way to fight poverty was also the simplest: give people money and trust them to decide what they need?

Since 2011, GiveDirectly has proven that idea at scale. We’ve delivered more than $1B in cash directly to 2+ million people living in poverty and crisis across 15 countries, and rigorous research shows the results: healthier kids, stronger businesses, sturdier homes, and more resilient families and local economies. Cash is now widely recognized as one of the most scalable, cost-effective, and dignified forms of aid.

Our ambition goes beyond our own programs. We want cash to become the benchmark for aid, much as the index fund became the benchmark for investing, so that every aid dollar is held to one question: is this doing more good than giving the money directly to people living in poverty?

We’re growing fast, and this is a rare and important moment to join.

We expect to hit $1B in revenue in 2026 with significant growth forecast for 2027. At the same time we are building a new technology stack and operating model designed for a roughly 10x change in scale, and we are actively pursuing partnerships with major funders to move even more money in bigger ways, to people who need it. We are known for our extensive integration of technology into field processes; our quantitative approach to performance measurement; and our commitment to rigorous, independent, experimental evaluation of our impact, with multiple Randomized Control Trials completed and others in progress.

How we work

Our team spans 20+ countries and 69 languages. Our culture is candid, analytical, and non-hierarchical. We expect high ownership and give people real responsibility early. Our values are central to how we hire, work, and grow, and they are deliberately opinionated:

  1. Recipients first. Recipients’ preferences come before those of donors or ourselves.
  2. Team next. We optimize for organizational success, not individual success.
  3. Be proactively candid. We say what we believe and share information openly.
  4. Create positive energy. We aim to be a source of energy for colleagues, not a drain.
  5. Think rigorously; act quickly. We reason from first principles, then act rather than debate.
  6. Know yourself and grow. We own our imperfections and seek feedback to grow.
  7. Accept reality. Propose solutions. We focus on what can change and bring solutions, not just problems.
  8. Be productively ambitious. We take risks for step-change impact, not incremental progress.

If they describe how you like to work and they energize you, this could be a great fit.

Want to learn more? Read and listen:

We are one of Time100’s Most Influential Companies of 2026, and our work has been covered by The Economist, NPR, TED, and The Washington Post. We're now preparing to deliver billions of dollars a year to people in extreme poverty, if funding allows. Read our CEO's essay on what that will take.

Reports to: Head of People

Level: Director

Location: Remote, but in a location that allows for at least ~3 hours of daily overlap with East Africa Time, and meaningful overlap with US Eastern hours. At this stage of GiveDirectly’s growth and scale, we’re prioritizing hiring in the countries below, where we can employ you through a GD entity or an established employer of record: Cameroon, Canada, Colombia, DRC, Germany, Ghana, Kenya, Malawi, Mozambique, Netherlands, Nigeria, Poland, Portugal, Rwanda, South Africa, Spain, Turkey, Uganda, United Kingdom, and United States. This list reflects where our employment infrastructure is established today, and may evolve as we grow. If you’re based elsewhere and not open to relocation, we may not be able to consider your application for this role right now, but we’d encourage you to check back. Please note that we are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of employment Visas in the U.S. or U.K. at this time.

Travel: Approximately 3-4 trips per year, including at least one to a country of operation and one to a key in-person leadership moment.

About this role

We are currently planning for a significant increase in scale, and we are building the People function that can carry it.

This is our first senior talent management role. Today we have pieces of talent management programs and processes in place, but not yet a function. You will build one: an intentional approach to how we onboard, develop, and retain our people. That covers performance management and its link to pay, manager and leadership development, learning, onboarding, talent planning and succession, employee listening and engagement, and culture and values.

The first year is weighted toward four priorities: joining the redesign of our performance system early, alongside the Head of People, and owning it as it moves into execution, as we move to pay for performance, revamping onboarding ahead of our next wave of hiring, planning our values retreat for senior leaders, and getting a read on employee listening and engagement. As those take shape, the balance shifts toward the longer-term build: the vision and roadmap for the function, a foundational manager program, talent planning and succession, and the team around you.

The reason for this weight: the performance system and onboarding are our most acute gaps today, but they should not be construed as a ceiling of the job. We are hiring a senior talent management leader who can shape the whole function over several years, not the owner of one or two programs. If your instinct on reading this is that the performance redesign is the whole job, this role probably isn’t the right fit, and the reverse is also true: if you want to set strategy but not build the first versions yourself, year one will frustrate you.

What you’ll do

Build the talent management function

  • Within your first 90 days, assess what exists today across these areas, recommend the sequencing for the first year, and agree to it with the Head of People.
  • Set the vision and multi-year roadmap for talent management across the areas it covers, and sequence the work against the People roadmap.
  • Propose the team around it, and decide what we build in-house and what we buy or borrow.
  • Connect talent management to workforce planning, compensation, and recruitment, in partnership with the Head of People, Finance, and function leaders.
  • Build an approach to talent and succession planning, starting with critical roles: work with leaders to identify succession gaps, assess potential successors, and put development plans in place to prepare people for future opportunities.

Own the performance system

  • Join the performance system redesign early, alongside the Head of People, and own it as it moves into execution: a system that produces reliable, calibrated outputs to inform merit increases, connected to our new salary bands.
  • Make the system worth using, not a check-the-box exercise: one that helps managers hold better performance and development conversations and gives employees clarity on expectations, feedback, and growth.
  • Build calibration and the data around it so ratings and merit decisions stay consistent and fair across countries, currencies, and manager quality.
  • Set a clear global standard for handling low performance that doesn’t default to a misconduct process, and equip managers to use it.
  • Ensure the performance system helps managers identify and support sustained high performance, connecting it to recognition, development, and career growth opportunities.
  • Iterate the system through multiple cycles, using calibration, outcome data, and feedback from managers and employees to improve it.

Build how people join, learn, and are led

  • Revamp onboarding ahead of our next wave of hiring: own the content and experience for new hires and their managers, working with People Ops on process and systems.
  • Build a foundational manager program and the tools behind it: feedback, coaching, difficult conversations, and performance management.
  • Extend into leadership development and broader learning as the function matures.

Shape culture and listen to employees

  • Plan the values retreat with an external facilitator and our executive sponsor, and own what carries into daily work afterward.
  • Get a read on listening and engagement today, covering what we hear, where it goes, and what should change, and use it to build our employee listening strategy.

What this role is not

  • Not a recruiting role. Hiring sits with our Talent Acquisition team. You partner with them on the handoff into onboarding and on how we assess and develop talent once people are here.
  • Not the owner of compensation design. Pay structures and bands are set through our compensation work. You own how performance is assessed and how ratings connect to pay decisions.
  • Not an employee relations or casework role. Cases in country belong to managers and HR Managers, supported by the People team. You own the performance system and the manager capability that helps them handle concerns well.
  • Not the owner of HR systems or process administration. Onboarding workflows and our HRIS sit with People Ops. You own the content and the experience.

Who we’re looking for

Required

  • 7+ years in talent management, performance, or organizational design roles, including time leading a function or a major part of one.
  • You have designed a performance system, not only administered one. You can show how ratings connected to pay and what you changed after the first cycle.
  • You have kept a rating and pay system fair across contexts with different currencies, labor markets, and manager quality.
  • You are a hands-on builder. You have built talent management programs and systems from scratch, or close to it, in a start-up or scale-up: performance, onboarding, manager development, or a whole function, where what you needed did not exist and you built it while the volume was already arriving. We are not looking for steady-state operating experience, or for leaders who have overseen this work without building it themselves.
  • You think in systems. You can show how a change in one part of a talent system, such as ratings, calibration, pay, promotion, or onboarding, shows up in the others, and you reason from the underlying problem rather than copying another organization’s template.
  • You design with change management in mind from the start. You plan for how managers and employees in different countries and cultures will adopt a new program or system as part of the design, not as a rollout step afterward, and can show how you knew it stuck rather than being worked around.
  • You have deep experience in at least two of onboarding, manager development, and employee engagement or listening, and working experience in the third. You have built programs and content people actually used, and can show how you knew they worked.
  • A track record of joining a major project already in motion, taking it over, and working through disagreement with a senior partner, and of influencing without formal authority in a matrixed organization.
  • Judgment and prioritization. You decide what slips and say so plainly.

Preferred

  • Experience in a mission-driven or international organization, ideally alongside high-growth commercial or tech experience.
  • Experience working across multiple countries, including sub-Saharan Africa.
  • Experience working with external facilitators, consultants, or vendors, and knowing what to hand off and what to hold.
  • Comfort using data (survey, performance, calibration) to make decisions, and knowing when the numbers mislead.
  • Exposure to compensation design or close work with a total rewards team.
  • Professional French or Portuguese.

Compensation

We also have a no negotiation policy to ensure we are paying staff equitably across roles. Hims & Hers is the leading health and wellness platform, on a mission to help the world feel great through the power of better health. We are redefining healthcare by putting the customer first and delivering access to care that is affordable, accessible, and personal, from diagnosis to treatment to delivery. No two people are the same, so we provide access to personalized care designed for results. By normalizing health & wellness challenges and innovating on their solutions, we’re making better health outcomes easier to achieve.

Hims & Hers is a public company, traded on the NYSE under the ticker symbol “HIMS.” To learn more about the brand and offerings, you can visit hims.com/about and hims.com/how-it-works . For information on the company’s outstanding benefits, culture, and its talent-first flexible/remote work approach, see below and visit www.hims.com/careers-professionals.

About the Role

Hims & Hers is looking for a Manager, HRIS to own our Dayforce systems strategy. This role carries direct people-management responsibility for our HRIS Analyst (based in the Philippines) and serves as the final approver for sensitive configuration changes, escalations, and system decisions.

This is a systems role and a stakeholder role in equal measure. You will sit at the intersection of HR, Payroll, Finance, and IT, gathering requirements from business partners and translating them into practical, right-sized system solutions - not the most elaborate build possible, but the one that solves the actual problem. You will be measured as much on how proactively and clearly you communicate and how well you manage relationships across the business as on your technical command of Dayforce.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own Dayforce systems strategy. Set direction for configuration of implemented modules (including Core HR and Time & Attendance), balancing stabilization needs against longer-term optimization and transformation priorities.

  • Manage the Dayforce HRIS Analyst. Directly manage the offshore HRIS Analyst, including workload prioritization, quality review, coaching, and performance management across a distributed, asynchronous working relationship.

  • Serve as final approver and escalation point. Retain approval authority for sensitive changes, ambiguous cases, and complex configuration decisions routed up from the analyst work queue.

  • Manage stakeholders proactively. Build and maintain trusted working relationships across HR, Payroll, Finance, and IT. Communicate status, risk, and trade-offs before being asked, not only when prompted.

  • Translate business requirements into MVP solutions. Partner with stakeholders to scope the smallest solution that meets the real business need, sequencing further enhancement deliberately rather than over-building on the first pass.

  • Govern integrations. Partner with IT and Security on integration and identity-provisioning issues, ensuring critical interfaces have clear ownership, monitoring, and escalation paths.

  • Oversee testing and UAT. Direct testing for system upgrades, releases, and new module rollouts, and ensure defects are logged, triaged, and resolved on schedule.

  • Maintain documentation as a single source of truth. Ensure business requirements, configuration workbooks, and process maps are kept current and are actually usable by the team.

  • Support global HRIS strategy. Partner with People Ops leadership on how international entities (currently on HiBob) fit into the broader HR systems landscape - including where integration with Dayforce makes sense and where the near-term goal is simply a reliable single source of truth for people data across systems.

Required Qualifications

  • 5+ years of hands-on Dayforce administration and configuration experience, including meaningful ownership of at least one full implementation (required).

  • Demonstrated experience managing or mentoring direct reports, ideally including remote or offshore staff working across time zones.

  • Strong, proven stakeholder management skills - a track record of building trust across HR, Payroll, Finance, and IT, and of communicating proactively rather than reactively. This is a core requirement for this role, not a soft preference.

  • Demonstrated ability to translate ambiguous business requirements into pragmatic, MVP-first technical solutions, with clear judgment about when to build now versus sequence for later.

  • Strong expertise in reporting, dashboards, and data analysis within Dayforce.

  • Experience supporting complex workforce environments (multi-location, high-volume, or multi-entity).

  • Strong working knowledge of core HR, payroll, and timekeeping processes and how they relate to system configuration and data.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the discipline to document decisions and keep stakeholders informed without prompting.

  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills, with disciplined attention to detail and accuracy.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience owning a Dayforce environment across the full arc from implementation through post-go-live stabilization and optimization.

  • Prior experience managing offshore or global-capability-center team members.

  • Familiarity with integrations, interfaces, SSO/identity provisioning, or data migrations, and the governance around them.

  • Experience executing formal UAT/regression testing and defect tracking programs.

  • Exposure to a healthcare, pharmacy, telehealth, or other regulated, high-volume environment.

  • Experience operating across more than one HRIS platform at once (e.g., following an acquisition or during a multi-entity rollout), including familiarity with HiBob or comparable systems.

From sourcing and licensing novel datasets to rigorous analysis and expert narrative framing, our teams ensure clients get not just data, but clarity and confidence.

We operate globally with offices in the US, APAC, and India. Our award-winning, people-centric culture—recognized by Inc. as a Best Workplace for three consecutive years—emphasizes transparency, ownership, and continuous mastery.

About The Role:

We are seeking a Senior Payroll & Benefits Administrator to own our US payroll operations and support the financial and administrative components of our benefits programs. You’ll be responsible for accurate and timely payroll for 500+ employees, multi-state payroll compliance, benefits invoice reconciliation, and the payroll and reconciliation processes associated with our self-insured health plans.

This is a highly hands-on role that will partner closely with Finance, People Ops, ADP, and our benefits partners. You’ll serve as an internal payroll subject matter expert while helping us strengthen controls, improve processes, and scale our payroll and benefits operations as the company grows.

This is a remote-friendly opportunity that can sit in NYC (where our headquarters is located), one of our office hubs, or anywhere else in the US. However, depending upon where the remote work is performed, income could be subject to New York State tax withholding.

We expect East Coast work hours.

As Our Senior Payroll & Benefits Administrator You Will:

  • Own end-to-end US payroll processing 500+ US employees, ensuring accurate, timely, and compliant payroll.
  • Partner with Finance and People Ops to manage payroll inputs and changes, including new hires, terminations, compensation changes, bonuses, deductions, and leaves, proactively identifying and resolving discrepancies.
  • Serve as the primary point of contact and internal subject matter expert for payroll, resolving employee questions and partnering with ADP and internal stakeholders on payroll, tax, and deduction issues.
  • Manage multi-state payroll and tax requirements for a distributed workforce, including appropriate handling of New York's Convenience of the Employer rule and related withholding requirements.
  • Own payroll and invoicing-related benefits administration, including employee deduction changes, QLEs, and ongoing coordination with the People Ops benefits team.
  • Review and reconcile benefits invoices and self-funded plan activity, validating employee eligibility, enrollment, payroll deductions, and plan fees, and partner with Accounting to resolve discrepancies and complete financial reconciliations.
  • Own payroll and benefits reconciliations and support month-end, year-end, W-2 preparation, open enrollment, benefits renewals, audits, and other recurring processes.
  • Maintain strong documentation and controls while identifying opportunities to automate, simplify, and scale payroll and benefits processes.

You Are Likely To Succeed If:

  • You have 4+ years of hands-on payroll and benefits administration experience, including direct responsibility for running payroll through ADP Workforce Now for a US workforce of at least 500 employees and managing multi-state payroll. Experience reconciling benefits invoices is required; experience with self-insured benefits plans and New York's Convenience of the Employer rule is strongly preferred.
  • You have strong working knowledge of federal, state, and local payroll and tax requirements and are comfortable researching and resolving complex payroll and withholding questions.
  • You have hands-on experience with benefits administration and invoice reconciliation and can confidently identify discrepancies across payroll, HRIS, carrier, and vendor data.
  • You are highly proficient with Excel or Google Sheets and comfortable working with large datasets, reconciliations, audits, and reporting.
  • You are exceptionally detail-oriented and take ownership of high-stakes, deadline-driven work, building appropriate checks and controls into your processes.
  • You are a clear, empathetic communicator who can independently own recurring processes, exercise good judgment, and continuously look for ways to make payroll and benefits administration more efficient, scalable, and reliable.

What We Offer:

Our compensation package includes comprehensive benefits, perks, and a competitive salary:

  • We care about your personal life, and we mean it. We offer flexible work hours, flexible vacation, a generous 401K match, parental leave, team events, wellness budget, learning reimbursement, and more!
  • Your growth at YipitData is determined by the impact that you are making, not by tenure, unnecessary facetime, or office politics. Everyone at YipitData is empowered to learn, self-improve, and master their skills in an environment focused on ownership, respect, and trust. See more on our high-impact, high-opportunity work environment above!
  • Base Salary Only: The annual base salary range for this position is anticipated to be $105,000-115,000. Final compensation may be determined by a number of factors, including, but not limited to, the applicant’s experience, knowledge, skills, abilities, and internal team benchmarks.
  • The compensation package also includes equity.

This role may be performed fully remotely within the United States. Please note that our US headquarters are located in NYC. If the remote work is performed outside of these offices, income may be subject to New York State tax withholding.

We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression, or veteran status. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer.
